title: Effect on caries of restricting sugars intake: systematic review to inform WHO guidelines
funder: The research was funded by Newcastle University's Centre for Oral Health Research.
authorConflicts: The authors declared no potential conflicts of interest.
result: 55 studies: 3 intervention, 8 cohort, 20 population and 24 cross-sectional. At least one positive association between sugars and caries in 42 of 50 studies in children and 5 of 5 in adults. Moderate-quality evidence (cohort studies) that caries is lower when free sugars intake is below 10% of energy; very-low-quality evidence (three Japanese national population studies) for a further reduction below 5%. In one Finnish cohort, DMFT was 0.5 with sucrose intake below 10% of energy and 1.4 above.
